VTS Scoring Log

Rebirth Labs

US-facing gray market· Lyophilized vials, nasal sprays, pills· Scored July 2026· rebirthlabs.org →

Rebirth Labs maintains a COA page listing 40+ compounds, which gives the appearance of a full documentation archive. On inspection, every link on that page resolves to a page anchor rather than an actual document - no COA is accessible. The site claims HPLC and mass spectrometry testing with no named lab. The score reflects a pattern of transparency infrastructure without transparency substance: the right signals are present as claims, but none are independently verifiable.

28 /100
Low Transparency
A COA page exists at a dedicated URL listing 40+ compounds, which is a positive structural signal. But the COA links on that page resolve to hash anchors rather than actual documents - a buyer clicking any COA link goes nowhere. Third-party testing is claimed with no named lab, no method detail, and no verifiable output. The infrastructure of transparency is present; the substance is not.

Scoring Notes
The broken COA page is the defining signal
A dedicated COA page listing 40+ compounds is more transparency infrastructure than many vendors build. The fact that every link resolves to a dead anchor rather than a document is the single most important finding in this score. It is not a technical oversight - linking 40+ products to placeholder anchors is a structural choice. A buyer who navigates to the COA page to verify their purchase gets nothing. That gap is the score.
What would change the score
Populating the COA page with actual documents, naming the testing lab, and adding lot-level traceability would move this score substantially. The structural commitment to a COA page is a real starting point - the content just needs to follow.
